dataset.name: learner-mistakes
dataset.description: Predicted mistake patterns for Class 1 Unit One learners (Maharashtra Board, Hindi/Marathi L1 backgrounds), with Miss Julie's gentle correction strategy for each. Patterns are grounded in the Unit One word banks (official 2025 textbook) and standard Hindi/Marathi-to-English transfer research knowledge; predicted error FORMS are marked as candidates until a human teacher reviews them against real classroom data.
usageRules: Miss Julie corrects ONE thing per turn — never a list.
The word 'wrong' is banned; corrections re-model and re-anchor.
Marathi kin terms (Aaji, Ajoba, Kaka, Kaki) are NOT mistakes — the textbook itself uses them; English role words are layered alongside.
Retroflexed 'r' and regional accents are NOT mistakes — only intelligibility issues are addressed, gently.
For SPEAKING_BEHAVIOUR items, the goal is participation first, production second.

editionVerification.title: English Balbharati — Grade One (2025)
editionVerification.note: Chapter references and target words verified against the official Unit One (printed pp.1-17).

mistakes.pattern: /v/ realised as /w/ (very → 'wery', everyone → 'eweryone')
mistakes.likelyCause: Hindi and Marathi lack a separate /v/-/w/ contrast; both map near [ʋ].
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Bite-lip cue: 'Gently touch your teeth to your lip — vvv.' Contrast pairs: van/wan played as a fun game, not a drill.
mistakes.languageNote: Do not overcorrect; [ʋ] is fully intelligible in Indian English.

mistakes.pattern: /z/ realised as /ʤ/ or /j/ (zebra → 'jebra')
mistakes.likelyCause: Devanagari ज covers both /j/ and /z/ in many speakers' mapping.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Bee-buzz game: 'Z is the bee's letter — /zzz/ like a bee in your mouth.'
mistakes.languageNote: zebra is a 1.5 word bank item.

mistakes.pattern: Short-vowel merger a/e/i (cat → 'ket', pen → 'pin')
mistakes.likelyCause: Hindi/Marathi vowel inventories do not split /æ-ɛ-ɪ/ the way English does.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Minimal-pair listening battles with pictures deciding the winner (cat/cot, pen/pin). Never lecture — the ears judge.
mistakes.languageNote: Directly targets 1.5's missing-vowel skill; expect improvement through the vowel work itself.

mistakes.pattern: Final consonant deletion (school → 'skoo', jump → 'jum')
mistakes.likelyCause: Many Marathi/Hindi words end in vowels; final stops are weak in the L1 phonology.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Clap-the-tail game: one clap for the head, one snap for the tail sound — 'skoo-L!'
mistakes.languageNote: school is a core 1.1 word; practise in the chant, not in isolation.

mistakes.pattern: Epenthetic vowel before s-clusters (school → 'iskool', stamp → 'istamp')
mistakes.likelyCause: L1 syllable structure resists /st-, sk-/ onsets.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Whisper-then-say: whisper 'sss-tamp' smoothly (whispering removes the extra vowel), then say it.
mistakes.languageNote: Whisper trick works well with young children.

mistakes.pattern: 'th' as /d/ or /t/ (the → 'da', Thank you → 'Tang you')
mistakes.likelyCause: Dental fricatives /θ, ð/ do not exist in Hindi or Marathi.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Accept meaning always; once per session model the tongue-between-teeth cue playfully ('peek-a-boo tongue'). Never block a polite moment for phonetics.
mistakes.languageNote: Indian English widely uses /t, d/ for 'th' — this is a low-priority polish item.

mistakes.pattern: /ʌ/ realised as /ʊ/ (jump → 'jump' with 'oo', up → 'oop')
mistakes.likelyCause: Hindi उ (/ʊ/) is the nearest vowel; /ʌ/ is absent.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Mouth-mirror: 'Open like a tiny crocodile — /ʌ/!' Contrast up/oop with the timeline picture (sun up vs balloon up).
mistakes.languageNote: get up, up us are 1.4/1.10 items.

mistakes.pattern: Letter-name reading instead of sound-blending (man read as 'em-ay-en')
mistakes.likelyCause: Letter names were learned first (1.3 teaches names AND sounds); child defaults to names.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Sound-box tapping: /m/ /a/ /n/ one tap each, then slide together. 'Letters are singers — they sing their sounds!'
mistakes.languageNote: Anticipated directly by 1.3→1.4 sequencing in the textbook.

mistakes.pattern: Missing vowel in writing/reading frame (s_n read as 'son', c_t as 'cut')
mistakes.likelyCause: Any vowel seems fillable; meaning is not yet driving the check.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Picture referee: say both candidate words aloud with their pictures; the picture picks the winner.
mistakes.languageNote: Directly the 1.5 exercise (s__n, c__t, f__sh, __gg, __wl).

mistakes.pattern: Article omission before singular nouns (I see dog → I see a dog)
mistakes.likelyCause: Hindi and Marathi have no articles; bare nouns are grammatical in L1.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: One-word bridge: echo back with just the article highlighted — 'a DOG! yes!' — never a rule speech.
mistakes.languageNote: Articles are taught in 1.6 ('Let us know' a/an/the).

mistakes.pattern: a/an swapped by spelling, not sound (a apple, an ball)
mistakes.likelyCause: Rule remembered as 'vowel letter' not 'vowel sound', or not remembered at all.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: First-sound test: say the word's beginning — /a/… /a-pple — special sound! So: an apple.
mistakes.languageNote: The book's own framing: 'an' for singular common noun beginning with vowels a, e, i, o, u.

mistakes.pattern: 'the' missed for unique things (sun → 'a sun')
mistakes.likelyCause: Unique-thing concept not yet formed in English; L1 uses demonstratives differently.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Boss-'the' story: only-one things (the sun, the sky, the Ganga, the Earth) wear the boss crown. Sort pictures into boss vs friends.
mistakes.languageNote: Book's exercise pairs: box, elephant, boy, apple, pen, Ganga, star, inkpot, umpire, octopus, Mars, hill.

mistakes.pattern: 'am/is/are' omitted in simple statements (I happy → I am happy)
mistakes.likelyCause: Hindi/Marathi zero-copula in present tense ('मैं खुश हूँ' keeps हूँ, but 'यह बड़ा है'-style ambiguity plus general dropping in child speech).
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Heartbeat 'am': 'Every I-sentence has a heartbeat word — I AM happy.' Tap chest while saying it.
mistakes.languageNote: Key 1.8 pattern 'I am ___' is the natural fix vehicle.

mistakes.pattern: Plural -s dropped after numbers (two bell → two bells)
mistakes.likelyCause: L1 numerals don't trigger plural marking.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Echo with emphasis: 'Two BELLSSS — two friends ringing together!' Count-with-fingers plus -s stretch.
mistakes.languageNote: Low priority at this stage; numbers appear in 1.2 (one-five).

mistakes.pattern: No capital letter for special names (priya, india, nagpur)
mistakes.likelyCause: Devanagari has no case distinction; the concept is new.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Capital-hat ritual: special names (people, cities, days) wear hats. Put a paper hat on the written name before rewriting it.
mistakes.languageNote: Directly asked by 1.8 ('Why do we use capital letters at the beginning of special names?').

mistakes.pattern: No capital letter / full stop at sentence boundaries
mistakes.likelyCause: Emergent writing stage; punctuation is not yet meaningful.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Sentence train: capital = engine, full stop = station. 'Where does your sentence train stop?'
mistakes.languageNote: Keep gentle — speech is the primary channel in Class 1; writing is emerging.

mistakes.pattern: Hindi inserted when the English word is unknown (यह… क्या है? patterns)
mistakes.likelyCause: Vocabulary gap; L1 is the thinking language.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Harvest-and-bridge: answer the need, give the English word once, resume in English. Hindi is a bridge, never a fault.
mistakes.languageNote: Matches the assignment's own model exchange pattern (Hindi word → English word → say it).

mistakes.pattern: Marathi inserted when English word is unknown (मला माहीत नाही)
mistakes.likelyCause: Vocabulary gap; honesty strategy for not knowing.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Honour the honesty, then shrink the question: 'Let us find out together — is it this one or this one?'
mistakes.languageNote: मला माहीत नाही = I don't know — a healthy thing to say; teach 'I don't know' as its English twin.

mistakes.pattern: Answers with the L1 object word instead of the English one (सेब/seb for apple — Hindi; शाळा for school — Marathi; example utterance uses the Marathi word)
mistakes.likelyCause: The concept is stored under its L1 label.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: The PM's model move, corrected for language attribution: 'Very good! Marathi madhye शाळा, Hindi mein vidyalay — and in English, school. Can you say school?' — accept, name the home language CORRECTLY (शाळा is Marathi only), then request the English word.
mistakes.languageNote: PM checkpoint-2 correction: an earlier draft said 'Hindi mein शाळा', but शाळा is Marathi. Hindi for school is विद्यालय / पाठशाला / स्कूल. The bridge pattern itself (accept, translate, request) is unchanged.

mistakes.pattern: Greeting register transferred without adjustment ( Namaste used with everyone, Hello unused)
mistakes.likelyCause: One respectful greeting serves all situations in L1.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Register game: elder cards get Namaste, friend cards get Hello/Hi. Both are polite — the game teaches choice, not correction.
mistakes.languageNote: The book itself pairs Hello (friends) with Namaste (elders) in 1.7.

mistakes.pattern: English kin terms resisted in favour of home terms (mother always 'आई', father always 'बाबा')
mistakes.likelyCause: Emotional attachment to kin terms; English labels feel distant.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Both-names rule: 'At home she is आई, in English class she is mother — your mother has two beautiful names.' Never force replacement.
mistakes.languageNote: The book models exactly this with Aaji/Ajoba sitting inside an English dialogue.

mistakes.pattern: Locomotion verbs swapped (skip/jump/run/walk mixed)
mistakes.likelyCause: All four map to one L1 motion concept at this age.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Body-first disambiguation: do the action, then name it; reversed check (Miss Julie acts silently, child names).
mistakes.languageNote: 1.1 word bank contains all four; the poem is the natural drilling ground.

mistakes.pattern: grin heard/produced as green
mistakes.likelyCause: Near-homophone; green is more frequent in child input.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Mouth-cue + contrast: grin = happy teeth show; green = colour of leaves. Two pictures, two words, quick fire.
mistakes.languageNote: Both are Unit One words (grin in 1.1, green in 1.6) — a designed contrast pair.

mistakes.pattern: Colour word used for every colour (favourite colour answer repeated for all bands)
mistakes.likelyCause: One strong word dominates; discrimination not yet built.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Colour-hunt with objects: touch something blue, something yellow — the world decides the word.
mistakes.languageNote: 1.6 gives seven bands; teach 3 first, grow the set.

mistakes.pattern: Verb chunk broken (I brush teeth → correct, but 'I brush the my teeth'-type overreach; more commonly 'I brush my tooth')
mistakes.likelyCause: Irregular plural of tooth unknown; singular/plural mapping incomplete.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Smile-mirror: 'How many teeth do you see? Many! Teeth — the team word.' One exposure per session; irregulars settle slowly.
mistakes.languageNote: teeth is a Help Box word in 1.10.

mistakes.pattern: b/d letter reversals (bat read as 'dat')
mistakes.likelyCause: Mirror-image confusion is developmentally normal at ages 5-6.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Belly cue: b has its belly on the right, d on the left. Trace while saying. Expect natural resolution; do not stress.
mistakes.languageNote: Letter shapes arise in 1.3-1.4 word building.

mistakes.pattern: Blends reduced in reading/spelling (stamp → 'samp', grin → 'gin')
mistakes.likelyCause: Consonant clusters are hard to segment in L1 phonology.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Stretched-words: 's-t-amp… stamp!' Tap per sound. Blend ladders (go → sto → stop) as a game.
mistakes.languageNote: st- and gr- appear in 1.1/1.2 word banks.

mistakes.pattern: Sight-word irregularity guesses (one read as 'o-ne', two as 't-woo')
mistakes.likelyCause: One/two are high-frequency irregular spellings; blending backfires.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Sight-word friends: these words are memorised as faces, not decoded. Flash-card faces with actions.
mistakes.languageNote: Number words enter via 1.2 actions.

mistakes.pattern: Silence on first prompt (shyness, not inability)
mistakes.likelyCause: New interface, new language, shared-lab visibility; affective filter high.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Channel ladder: action → point → whisper → voice. Any channel counts as an answer; praise the step, not the volume.
mistakes.languageNote: The SILENT learner path across all chapters implements this ladder.

mistakes.pattern: Guessing repeatedly without listening (random word for every prompt)
mistakes.likelyCause: Guessing has previously been rewarded by chance, or the task feels unbounded.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Shrink the field: two choices with visible referents; require a look-listen-decide beat before every answer.
mistakes.languageNote: GUESSING_REPEATEDLY path in every chapter implements two-choice re-anchoring.

mistakes.pattern: One-word answers only; resists sentence production
mistakes.likelyCause: Production cost of sentences is high; one word feels sufficient.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Two-word ladder: accept the word, offer the frame with a gap — 'I go to ___.' Fill-in-together, then solo.
mistakes.languageNote: Pattern completion, not demand: the frame does half the work.

mistakes.pattern: Echoes without understanding (repeats the model, fails the reversed check)
mistakes.exampleUtterance: (repeats 'The bell rings' perfectly; cannot name the word when Miss Julie points at a bell)
mistakes.likelyCause: Echo is a low-cost strategy that mimics success.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: VERIFY stage discipline: reverse the direction (act→word, picture→word, new-listener retell). Mastery only after an independent use.
mistakes.languageNote: This is why Miss Julie never declares mastery on a first correct answer (assignment requirement).

mistakes.pattern: Speaks too quietly for the microphone (ASR fails)
mistakes.likelyCause: Shyness; unclear mic expectations in shared labs.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Big-voice game: 'Talk to the rainbow!' — imagine the mic is a friend far away. Practise loud-soft switches for fun first.
mistakes.languageNote: Backend hint: retry prompt should model the target volume, not just re-ask.

mistakes.pattern: Words run together too fast for recognition (wannagotoschool)
mistakes.likelyCause: Excitement; L1 rhythm transferred to English.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Turtle-race: 'Turtle words win today — slow and proud.' Clap per word while saying.
mistakes.languageNote: Also helps ASR accuracy materially.

mistakes.pattern: False confidence: says 'yes yes' to comprehension checks without understanding
mistakes.exampleUtterance: Yes yes! (then cannot act the instruction)
mistakes.likelyCause: Social politeness; fear of appearing lost.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Do-don't-say checks: comprehension is verified by actions ('Show me!') not by yes/no. No shame — the action IS the fun.
mistakes.languageNote: Book's Activity Time (1.9 cap folding) is a natural do-check environment.

mistakes.pattern: Gender agreement transferred into English pronoun choices (he/she swaps for people)
mistakes.exampleUtterance: This is my mother. He is making food.
mistakes.likelyCause: Hindi grammatical gender (माँ = feminine but verb agreement differs in structure); pronoun mapping is not one-to-one.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Anchor pairs with photos: 'Mother — she. Father — he.' Picture-tap game she/he, two rounds only per session.
mistakes.languageNote: Low priority inside Unit One (pronouns not formally taught); fix in passing, never as the lesson focus.

mistakes.pattern: Interrupts / answers before the prompt finishes (shared-lab turn-taking)
mistakes.likelyCause: Group excitement; lab setting removes natural turn cues.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Listening-ears ritual: finger on ear, count two heartbeats, THEN answer. Make the wait a game, not a rule.
mistakes.languageNote: Book's outcome mapping includes 'waits for his/her turn to speak' (learning outcome 9.3).

mistakes.pattern: Question word order lost (What is your name → 'Your name is what?' or statement-only)
mistakes.likelyCause: L1 question formation (क्या तुम्हारा नाम…? / तुझं नाव काय?) maps differently.
mistakes.correctionStrategy: Question melody: sing the English question with a rising end — 'What is your naaame?' Melody carries the order better than a rule.
mistakes.languageNote: 1.8's question is a core outcome; melody-first, analysis never.
